# Zeeshan Anjum Junaidi

Senior software engineer based in Karachi, Pakistan. Works on infrastructure
and platform engineering at IDWise: Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD and network
security across AWS and GCP, behind identity verification and anti-money-
laundering systems.

Outside work, builds simulation engines and interactive technical tools. The
Lab and the writing below are personal exploration, not professional
employment experience. Robotics, spaceflight and control-systems material on
this site is self-directed study, not part of the job described above.

## Writing

- [Landing a Booster](https://zeeshananjum.com/writing/landing-a-booster/): eleven sections on returning a first stage to a pad. State vector, translational and rotational dynamics, gimbal and grid-fin allocation, ZEM/ZEV guidance, numerics.
- [The Tsiolkovsky rocket equation](https://zeeshananjum.com/writing/tsiolkovsky-rocket-equation/): deriving the rocket equation from momentum conservation, and what it means for staging and engine choice.
- [The transactional outbox](https://zeeshananjum.com/writing/transactional-outbox/): why a database write and an event publish cannot both succeed, and the ordering bug most implementations ship with.

## Lab

Interactive tools, each running in the browser with no backend.

- [Rocket Landing](https://zeeshananjum.com/lab/rocket-landing/): three.js powered-descent simulator. Thrust, drag, fuel burn, autopilot and manual flight.
- [SLAM Playground](https://zeeshananjum.com/lab/slam-playground/): simultaneous localization and mapping. Noisy LiDAR, GPS and IMU, occupancy-grid mapping, ICP scan matching.
- [Hybrid A* Parking](https://zeeshananjum.com/lab/hybrid-astar-parking/): path planning over reachable vehicle states rather than grid cells, including reverse-parking maneuvers.
- [Back of the Envelope](https://zeeshananjum.com/lab/back-of-the-envelope/): system design capacity calculator. Traffic, storage, cache, bandwidth, compute, sharding, queues, latency, cost, plus a diagram tool.
